blinding_note: the v3 packet's ids named the model ("gemma-3n-e2b-it::gate1_validation:..."), so v3 blinded the verdict but not the model label. This packet mints opaque ids and keeps the mapping in the sealed key.
classification: Gate 1 input evidence. No session started. Author labels are diagnostic evidence and §10.4 hierarchy input, NEVER independent validation.

controls.shortfall_note: A:fail:margin_larger is 7 of 8 discordant, so matched concordant controls do not exist in that stratum; the shortfall is topped up from the concordant pool at large and recorded rather than hidden

outstanding_before_a_session_can_run: the tool-assisted marking interface: §10.3 requires the annotator to mark each qualifying feature with the interface tallying the annotator's OWN marks, and the v3 review app takes a bare S/V/U judgment instead. This is the registered fix for v3's failure mode -- all four v3 disagreements were unaided off-by-one counting errors at margin one, and four independent recounts reproduced the verifier every time.
a B-class reviewer definition set: the v3 definitions are A-specific (an occurrence-count instruction) and 1 of the 22 items is B-class
explicit researcher agreement to run the session
protocol_properties_required: blind: no arm, model label, companion, verifier verdict or other annotator's work visible
tool-assisted marking, no automatic detection or counting
fail-class stratification by realised margin, reported separately

rejected_sizing.rule: §10.3, min(150, N_c) per class per instrument
rejected_sizing.why_rejected: §10.3 requires an annotator independent of the design and analysis team; the annotator is the study author, so the basis stays HUMAN_VALIDATION_UNAVAILABLE however many items are labelled
